GS-SYNC-001.impact: A peer can exceed the intended bound on retained page descriptors and IDs for one open run. Per-frame decoding limits do not bound aggregate run memory. Existing traffic-governor and deadline gaps make a receiver-owned cap especially necessary, but this defect exists independently of their fixes.
GS-SYNC-001.proof: Independent Android owner probe adopts a digest, opens a run, and sends 65 valid increasing one-ID pages with done=0. The 65th is Accepted. The receiver appends to delivered and increments pagesReceived without checking MAX_PAGES_PER_RUN or an outstanding request. The sender-side pump limit does not constrain a peer’s incoming pages. Swift has the matching unchecked append.
remediation_steps: Keep inventoryReceiverMustEnforce64PageRunLimit as a receiver-boundary regression; do not call pump helpers to enforce limits on behalf of the remote peer.

Track the exact outstanding inventory request under the relation owner: snapshot, generation, exclusive cursor and allowed response count. Refuse unsolicited or replayed pages without growing any retained collection.

Before appending a page or advancing the cursor, enforce received pages <=64 and the frozen per-run requested-message/retained-ID budget. Reject the first over-budget page before mutation and end/defer that run with a typed result.

Make page admission, cursor advancement, pending-want calculation and token revalidation one serialized transition. Reads that suspend must stage their result and revalidate the captured relation generation before committing it.
Bound delivered, wantQueue and per-peer relation state explicitly; release run-owned buffers/leases on done, timeout, reset, disconnect and cancellation.

Provide a bounded next-turn continuation that preserves reconciliation progress for larger inventories, rather than repeatedly restarting at the first page. Test convergence across run limits as well as small bloom-collision fixtures.
GS-SYNC-001.title: Inventory receiver accepts more than its bounded run page budget

closure_tests: Port testPingReplyRemainsBoundToRequestingPeer and retain both assertions: C receives zero PING replies, B still receives one. Keep testSamePeerPingPositiveControl green.

GS-SYNC-002.impact: Link-local PING, inventory and WANT responses lose their destination. An unrelated peer turn can consume the answer, leaving the requesting peer unanswered and mixing separate reconciliation runs.
GS-SYNC-002.proof: Audit003SyncTests sends a PING from B into A, drains A for C, then for B. C receives the sole PING reply; B receives zero. The same-peer positive control passes. Android has the same global control-outbox design. sync-final-probes.log records two failed assertions for this case.
remediation_steps: Change the outbox element from FrameV2 alone to a control reply containing destination NodeID, immutable relation identity/generation and frame. Set these fields at the ingress decision, while the requesting relation is known.

Change offerControlFrames to require that destination context. Pass it from handleControlFrame/ingestInbound and every other response producer. Do not recover the recipient later from whichever peer is being drained.

Drain only entries belonging to the requested current relation. Preserve replies for other live peers. Drop entries for retired generations on disconnect; never migrate old replies to a replacement relation with the same NodeID.
Bound both per-peer entries/bytes and aggregate control memory. Document refusal/backpressure when full; do not silently erase another peer’s progress to make room.
Revalidate ownership at writer admission as in GS-RUNTIME-001. Apply the same types and semantics to Android and Swift.
GS-SYNC-002.title: A control reply for one peer is drained by another peer

GS-UX-001.impact: Users cannot execute the claimed contact verification, compose/send, hold-to-confirm SOS or resumable wipe journeys. Passing a model test with a fake port does not show a user action reaches a durable authority.
GS-UX-001.proof: Android production port implementations are UnavailableTrustPort/UnavailableMeshPort; other implementations are test fakes. MeshScreens renders draft and SOS instructions as Text without editable controls, gesture callbacks or onCommand wiring. The model is read once with uiState(), without observable Compose state. Swift authority protocols and their model initializers have only test construction; no lab SwiftUI journey consumes them. See source-caller-searches.txt.
remediation_steps: After GS-LAB-001, put the usable lab UI in the lab target or a UI module explicitly included there. Do not enable mesh in the shipping Archive graph.

Implement TrustPort/MeshPort (and Swift authority ports) as adapters to the one runtime’s real durable identity, delivery, inbox and wipe owners. Translate typed failures; never mutate a UI-only map as a substitute for the repository CAS.

Expose observable state: StateFlow collected with lifecycle on Compose, and MainActor observable state consumed by SwiftUI. Refresh after durable events and lifecycle restoration, and unsubscribe when the owner ends.

Add a real recipient selector, UTF-8-bounded text input and Send action. Wire retry, explicit fingerprint compare/confirm, exact rotation-candidate approval and revoke actions to their existing command types.

Implement SOS as an actual cancellable hold gesture with a monotonic confirmation threshold and accessible alternative. A label reading Hold is not a gesture. Release/cancel before threshold must not author a call; active cancel must show the relay-copy limitation.
Restore active calls, conversations, pending rotations and wipe progress from the real reopened store. Apply protected-data unavailability and permission explanations from actual platform state.
Add navigation and meaningful accessibility semantics; exercise the rendered controls rather than setting model state directly.
